scope: Additive multiplyNumberUnboxed and factor-independent m80 split cache. Only the2010 floating evaluator consumes the new Number-or-Float80 return; existing public method bodies retain their previous API.
checks: The new method uses the same PC53 normal/exact-zero tests and the same bounded mixed-product rounding-cell certificate as multiplyNumber. Every uncertified, extended, nonfinite or other-precision case uses the same original operand boxing and multiplication fallback.

The WeakMap key is private normalized parts owned by an immutable Float80 value. Cached high/tail/ah/al are exact factor-independent values produced by the unchanged expressions; every range guard runs before lookup.
The cache does not store factors/products/results or retain dead inputs. Per-factor Dekker correction, midpoint asymmetry, error margin and final sign operations are unchanged.
2010 fpMul retains operand unboxing order and consumes an exact Number directly. Extended fallback values are still unboxed only when exactNumber proves representability.

Exact Float80 prototypes select the new unboxed method. Extended subclass operands retain the previous dynamic multiplyNumber lookup, receiver, return and exception contract; both operand orders are covered.
performanceScope: The source-only cached-split prototype measured2.57times the uncached unboxed leaf throughput on repeatedly reused immutable inputs. This is not a browser FPS result.

resolvedFindings.issue: Switching fpMul to the additive method could bypass a Float80 subclass override of multiplyNumber.
resolvedFindings.fix: Use the unboxed method only for the exact standard prototype; preserve the old method on subclass operands.
